body.p: The processes most Oxygen XML Editor/Author editor variables.
body.note:
The editor variables support is context-specific. When an author creates a file from the New File wizard, Web Author expands editor variables from the template into the newly created file. A variable that works in Oxygen XML Editor/Author desktop or in an Author action might not work in a Web Author template.
The ${ask(...)} variable does not prompt during New File creation and stays unexpanded in the newly created file. Use defaults in the template or move the prompt to an Author action after the file opens. The ${ask(...)} variable is still valid in Web Author actions and operation arguments, such as InsertFragmentOperation.
body.p:
The supported editor variables are:
${ask('message', type, ('real_value1':'rendered_value1'; 'real_value2':'rendered_value2'; ...), 'default_value')} - To prompt for values at runtime, use the ask('message', type, ('real_value1':'rendered_value1'; 'real_value2':'rendered_value2'; ...), 'default-value'') editor variable. You can set the following parameters:
'message' - The displayed message. Note the quotes that enclose the message.
'default-value' - Optional parameter. Provides a default value.
type - Optional parameter, with one of the following values:The dialog box title is based on the parameter type:
For url and relative_url parameters, the title is the parameter name followed by the 'message' value.
For the other parameters listed below, the title is the parameter name.
If no parameter is used, the title will be "Input".
Parameter
url Format: ${ask('message', url, 'default_value')}
Description: The input is treated as a URL. checks that the provided URL is valid.
Example:
${ask('Input URL', url)} - The displayed dialog box has the name Input URL. The expected input type is URL.
${ask('Input URL', url, 'http://www.example.com')} - The displayed dialog box has the name Input URL. The expected input type is URL. The input field displays the default value http://www.example.com.
password Format: ${ask('message', password, 'default')}
Description: The input is hidden with bullet characters.
Example:
${ask('Input password', password)} - The displayed dialog box has the name 'Input password' and the input is hidden with bullet symbols.
${ask('Input password', password, 'abcd')} - The displayed dialog box has the name 'Input password' and the input hidden with bullet symbols. The input field already contains the default abcd value.
generic Format: ${ask('message', generic, 'default')}
Description: The input is treated as generic text and requires no special handling.
Example:
${ask('Hello world!')} - The dialog box has a Hello world! message displayed.
${ask('Hello world!', generic, 'Hello again!')} - The dialog box has a Hello world! message displayed and the value displayed in the input box is 'Hello again!'.
relative_url Format: ${ask('message', relative_url, 'default')}
Description: Input is considered a URL. tries to make the URL relative to that of the document you are editing.If the $ask editor variable is expanded in content that is not yet saved (such as an untitled file, whose path cannot be determined), then will transform it into an absolute URL.
Example:
${ask('File location', relative_url, 'C:/example.txt')} - The dialog box has the name 'File location'. The URL inserted in the input box is made relative to the currently edited document location.
combobox Format: ${ask('message', combobox, ('real_value1':'rendered_value1';...;'real_valueN':'rendered_valueN'), 'default')}
Description: Displays a dialog box that offers a drop-down menu. The drop-down list contains the specified rendered_value values. Selecting a value returns its associated real_value.The 'default' parameter specifies the default-selected value and can match either a key or a value.
Example:
${ask('Operating System', combobox, ('win':'Microsoft Windows';'macos':'macOS';'lnx':'Linux/UNIX'), 'macos')} - The dialog box has the name 'Operating System'. The drop-down menu displays the three given operating systems. Based on your selection, the associated value is returned. In this example, the default value is indicated by the osx key. However, the same result could be obtained if the default value is indicated by Mac OS, as in the following example: ${ask('Operating System', combobox, ('win':'Microsoft Windows';'macos':'Mac OS';'lnx':'Linux/UNIX'), 'macOS')}
${ask('Mobile OS', combobox, ('win':'Windows Mobile';'ios':'iOS';'and':'Android'), 'Android')}
editable_combobox Format: ${ask('message', editable_combobox, ('real_value1':'rendered_value1';...;'real_valueN':'rendered_valueN'), 'default')}
Description: Displays a dialog box that offers a drop-down menu with editable elements. The drop-down list contains the specified real_value values. You can select an option or enter a custom value in the text field.The 'default' parameter specifies the default-selected value and can match either a key or a value.rendered_value type of values are ignored.
Example:
${ask('Operating System', editable_combobox, ('win':'Microsoft Windows';'macos':'macOS';'lnx':'Linux/UNIX'), 'macos')} - The dialog box has the name 'Operating System'. The drop-down menu displays the three given operating systems and also allows you to edit the entry. The associated value will be returned based based on your selection or the text you enter.
radio Format: ${ask('message', radio, ('real_value1':'rendered_value1';...;'real_valueN':'rendered_valueN'), 'default')}
Description: Displays a dialog box that offers a series of radio buttons. Each radio button displays a 'rendered_value and will return an associated real_value.The 'default' parameter specifies the default-selected value and can match either a key or a value.
Example:
${ask('Operating System', radio, ('win':'Microsoft Windows';macos:'macOS';'lnx':'Linux/UNIX'), 'macos')} - The dialog box has the name 'Operating System'. The radio button group allows you to choose between the three operating systems.In this example, macOS is the default-selected value and if selected, it would return macos for the output.
${configured.ditaot.dir} - The default directory of the DITA Open Toolkit distribution.
${frameworkDir(fr_name)} - The path (as file path) of the fr_name framework.
${i18n(key)} - Editor variable used only at framework-level to allow translating names and descriptions of Author mode actions in multiple actions.
${user.name} - Evaluates to the name of the current user. Can be used only as an argument to com.oxygenxml.username.InsertFragmentOperation, which is contributed by this plugin: . The ${author.name} editor variable is not supported in .

section.p: These variables look similar, but the suffix determines whether the value is expanded as a URL or as a local file path:

section.p: In this section, framework covers both the built-in frameworks and user-uploaded framework extensions. The example column shows values for a user-uploaded extension. For a built-in framework, the variables point to the matching folder under frameworks.
Use the URL form when the target expects a URL (for example, when registering framework CSS files):
Use the file path form when the target expects a local directory path (for example, when registering document templates):
section.note: Do not treat the URL and file path forms as interchangeable. A common failure is using ${framework} where Web Author expects a file system path. On Windows, this expands to a value such as file:/D:/.../templates/Topic. Some loaders pass that string to file access code without removing the file: prefix, and Web Author logs a security error, such as: Templates directory cannot be accessed: file:/D:/.../templates/Topic java.security.AccessControlException: access denied ("java.io.FilePermission" "file:\D:\...\templates\Topic" "read")
